defect.locator_note: content_page.md treatment section and lake treatment.derivation.lane2_top_cited
defect.problem: The good-law call itself matches the lake judgment field, but the page states treatment too categorically because the disclosed lake record also shows proposed negative-treatment edges and an unresolved top-cited-lane audit marker. The displayed treatment should distinguish final treatment from pending/proposed audit signals.
defect.proposed_fix: Retain good_law as of 2026-06-30, but change the public treatment note to something like: good law as of 2026-06-30; disclosed treatment audit has no finalized negative treatment of Bailey, but proposed/mentioned progeny edges remain pending audit. Avoid the categorical sentence 'No negative treatment of Bailey' unless the audit is complete.

reasons: Lake treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30 and varies_by_point is false, so the core good-law label survives.
All listed treatment edges have field_iii set to mentioned and proposed true, so the disclosed record does not show a finalized overruling, abrogation, or supersession of Bailey.
But lane2_top_cited has audit_needed true, cap_hit true, and audit_marker R15 treatment audit required; that creates a treatment-currency caveat the page should surface.
residual_risks: The unresolved treatment audit could later downgrade or qualify the good-law status.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Clarify 'no finalized negative treatment in this record' rather than 'No negative treatment of Bailey.'
